chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is the prayer offered over the deceased in the mosque? He said, 'Yes.'
Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (the Imams), both upon them be peace:

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Aban ibn Uthman, a prominent narrator
key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: Peace be upon them (referring to the two Imams in the chain)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: Prayer offered over the deceased (Funeral Prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform the funeral prayer inside the mosque in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility of performing the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) within the mosque, a ruling supported by the chain of narrators including Aban ibn Uthman and Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the mosque is a valid venue for the communal prayer over the deceased, distinguishing it from other acts of worship that may have specific location restrictions. The corroborating report from Muhammad ibn Muslim further solidifies the consistency of the Imams' position on this matter.
